html:
Lake Chad, a large shallow lake shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria, shrank sharply from the 1960s, by some estimates losing about nine tenths of its open water by the end of the century.

Its size has always swung with the rains, and it was far larger when the Sahara was green. The Sahel droughts of the 1970s and 1980s, and more water taken for irrigation, split it into a southern pool and marshes. Fishermen, farmers and herders followed the water, and disputes grew over land that appeared. Since 2009 the Boko Haram insurgency has made the islands and shores a war zone. See also the Sao and Kanem-Bornu.
sum: Lake Chad, a large shallow lake shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria, shrank sharply from the 1960s, by some estimates losing about nine tenths of its open water by the end of the century.
